top_events.title: Several ships attacked in Strait of Hormuz as Iran launches fresh strikes - TradeWinds News

analysis.summary: The headline reports attacks on several ships in the Strait of Hormuz amid fresh Iranian strikes. This raises the risk of tanker disruption and tighter effective crude flows through a critical chokepoint, supporting an oil-price risk premium. Operational details and duration are not provided.
analysis.why_xom: Potentially higher crude prices and geopolitical risk can support upstream earnings expectations for Exxon Mobil, although actual XOM impact depends on the duration of disruption, production exposure, and broader market conditions.

top_events.title: Three vessels attacked in Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday: UKMTO - Türkiye Today

analysis.summary: UKMTO reported attacks on three vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. The incident raises the risk of tanker disruption, route avoidance, insurance costs, and potential interruptions to crude flows, but the supplied report does not confirm a physical supply outage.
analysis.why_xom: Higher geopolitical and Hormuz disruption risk can support crude prices and benefit Exxon Mobil through stronger upstream realizations, though shipping disruption could also raise logistics and operating risks.

top_events.title: Several ships attacked in Strait of Hormuz as Iran launches fresh strikes - TradeWinds News

analysis.summary: Reported attacks on several ships in the Strait of Hormuz during fresh Iranian strikes raise the risk premium for crude and tanker traffic. The headline does not confirm a closure, cargo loss, or sustained supply disruption.
analysis.why_xom: Higher geopolitical risk and potential crude-price support could benefit Exxon Mobil’s upstream earnings, although actual supply interruptions or shipping constraints could also create downstream and operational pressures.

top_events.title: Attacks Cut Saudi Oil Output and East-West Pipeline Flow, State News Agency Says - EnergyNow.com

analysis.summary: A state news agency reports that attacks reduced Saudi oil output and disrupted flow through the East-West pipeline. This indicates a potentially material near-term tightening of crude supply, although the headline provides no magnitude or duration.
analysis.why_xom: Higher crude prices from a Saudi supply disruption could support Exxon Mobil’s upstream earnings and cash flow. The effect is indirect, and the headline does not identify any impact on XOM-operated assets.

top_events.title: Attacks Cut Saudi Oil Output and East-West Pipeline Flow, State News Agency Says - energynow.com

analysis.summary: Saudi oil output and East-West pipeline flows were reportedly reduced following attacks, according to a state news agency. This indicates a potential direct crude-supply and transportation disruption, though the headline provides no outage magnitude or duration.
analysis.why_xom: A reduction in Saudi production and pipeline flows could support global crude prices, benefiting XOM's upstream earnings. The impact is partly uncertain because the scale and persistence of the disruption are unspecified.

top_events.title: Hormuz at Near Standstill as Iran Warns Ships to Keep to its Waters - energynow.com

analysis.summary: The headline reports near-stagnant shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and an Iranian warning to vessels, implying a potentially significant disruption to crude transport and regional energy flows. No additional operational details are provided.
analysis.why_xom: A sustained Hormuz disruption could support crude prices, potentially benefiting Exxon Mobil's upstream earnings, although broader geopolitical and market risks could offset some benefit.

log_health.last_line: 2026-09-30 13:25:38,807 | INFO | feed updated | new=6 active=301 signal=+0.397 adjustment=+3.97

review.summary: The paper system operated within its configured exposure, position, trade-count, and daily-loss controls, but same-day evidence is insufficient for model calibration. Activity was sparse: 23 funnel records produced 3 accepted paper orders and one realized AAPL loss of $2.25. Signals were strongly buy-skewed, concentrated in TSLA, while the four-position cap blocked six submissions. Regime, premarket, VIX, geo, and ZPTA observations lack enough matched forward outcomes for causal conclusions. No trading thresholds or risk caps should be changed today.
findings: Observed: 3,325 decisions consisted of 3,316 HOLD, 8 BUY, and 1 SELL actions. The funnel reports 22 raw threshold crossings, approximately 0.66% of decision rows, although its side counts total 23 (22 BUY and 1 SELL); this reconciliation mismatch should be investigated.

Observed: Signal direction was highly asymmetric. TSLA generated 5 of 8 BUY decisions; AAPL generated the only SELL and one BUY. Only AAPL and TSLA received same-day orders. Hypothesis: the imbalance may reflect the day's bullish conditions rather than threshold bias; one day cannot distinguish these explanations.

Observed: Confirmation filtered 14 funnel records, while the maximum-open-position gate blocked 6 submissions. Three submissions were accepted without submit failures. The dashboard showed four open positions and $8,233.08 exposure, below the $10,000 exposure cap. There is no evidence supporting relaxation of the four-position cap.

Observed: Realized evidence is only one closed AAPL paper trade with a $2.25 loss. Unrealized results at the dashboard snapshot were mixed across AMZN, SPY, TSLA, and XOM. This sample cannot support changes to entry, exit, stop-loss, take-profit, or confirmation settings.

Observed: Market-regime SHADOW produced 74 observations, all RISK_ON with score 100, and 22 associated decisions all allowed equity. There is no contrasting regime sample, so regime effectiveness or calibration cannot be evaluated.

Observed: VIX was 16.17 and below the regime stress condition. Average VIX adjustments were small across symbols, ranging from about -0.022 to +0.008, but no matched counterfactual or forward-outcome evidence isolates their effect.

Observed: The geo feed was live and contributed materially to energy-linked scoring: XOM averaged a +3.221 geo adjustment and GLD +0.804, while other symbols averaged zero. Several top headlines appear to describe duplicate underlying Hormuz or Saudi supply events. Hypothesis: duplicate-event concentration may overstate geo evidence, but the supplied data do not establish the deduplication behavior or outcome impact.

Observed: Premarket intelligence produced five BULLISH snapshots with score 75, small positive SPY and QQQ gaps, and RISK_ON regime. Social sentiment was explicitly unavailable. Dashboard signals showed zero premarket adjustment later in the day, consistent with an expired active window, but no opening-window outcome ledger was supplied.

Observed: Financial-leverage SHADOW was enabled but produced zero snapshots, signals, and outcomes. XLF, FAS, and FAZ premarket gaps were also null. Consequently, there is no evidence to assess the configured score floor of 70 or any leveraged-financial candidate behavior.

Observed: ZPTA SHADOW model/horizon cells have only 7 or 8 samples, below the minimum calibration target of 12. Continuation, pullback, and VWAP-reclaim results were weak in these tiny samples, while no shadow trades closed. The latest provider was yahoo_delayed and the latest status was NO_NEW_BAR, so threshold changes would be premature.

Evidence gap: Forward returns are not supplied for ordinary threshold crossings, rejected candidates, regime decisions, VIX adjustments, geo adjustments, or premarket bias. This prevents attribution of outcomes to individual model components.

proposals.title: Reconcile funnel counts and attach forward outcomes to every threshold event
proposals.current: The funnel reports 22 raw threshold crossings, but BUY/SELL side counts total 23. Records show gate dispositions but no matched 5/15/30/60-minute forward returns for accepted, confirmation-filtered, or position-cap-blocked events.
proposals.proposed: Add a stable event ID linking decision, threshold crossing, confirmation state, gate result, order attempt, and fill. Enforce and report count invariants, including raw crossings by side. In SHADOW, record 5/15/30/60-minute forward returns and score components for every crossing, including blocked candidates. Do not alter thresholds, confirmations, portfolio caps, or order behavior until at least 12 resolved observations exist for the evaluated segment.
evidence: The reported raw-crossing count is 22 while funnel side counts sum to 23.
Fourteen records awaited confirmation, six were blocked by MAX_OPEN_POSITIONS, and three produced submitted orders.
Only one realized trade exists, so accepted-order P/L cannot evaluate the larger candidate set.
proposals.risk: Low implementation risk if logging is asynchronous. Incorrect event joins could misattribute outcomes, so invariant failures should be surfaced without affecting paper orders.

proposals.title: Restore XLF/FAS/FAZ financial-leverage SHADOW data capture
proposals.current: The feature is enabled with a minimum score of 70 and outcome horizons of 5,15,30,60 minutes, but it generated zero snapshots, signals, or outcomes. Premarket XLF/FAS/FAZ gaps were null and the dashboard reported FINANCIAL_SNAPSHOT_UNAVAILABLE.
proposals.proposed: Add per-symbol quote/bar diagnostics for XLF, FAS, and FAZ, including provider, timestamp, bar age, missing-field reason, and IEX entitlement/coverage status. Permit a configured research-only fallback data provider if primary data are unavailable, while labeling provider and latency. Resume SHADOW snapshots and horizon outcomes only; retain the 70 score floor and prohibit paper order routing from this module.
evidence: Financial-leverage snapshot_rows, signal_rows, and outcome_rows were all zero.
The latest candidate was null and the dashboard reason was FINANCIAL_SNAPSHOT_UNAVAILABLE.
All three financial ETF premarket gaps were null.
proposals.risk: Fallback data may differ in latency or price construction from IEX. Provider identity and bar age must therefore remain part of every observation.

proposals.title: Run a deduplicated geo-adjustment counterfactual alongside the active score
proposals.target: Geo-feed event aggregation for XOM and GLD
proposals.current: The geo feed had 301 active events and a +3.97 current adjustment. XOM averaged +3.221 and GLD +0.804. The top-event list contains repeated or near-duplicate reports of the same incidents, but deduplication details and component outcomes are unavailable.
proposals.proposed: Cluster geo headlines by normalized incident, publication time, category, and source lineage. Log raw-event count, unique-cluster count, source concentration, active adjustment, and a deduplicated SHADOW adjustment side by side. Capture XOM and GLD forward returns at 5/15/30/60 minutes after material cluster changes. Do not replace the active adjustment or tune its cap from this one-day sample.
evidence: Multiple top entries repeat the TradeWinds Hormuz attack report and the EnergyNow Saudi output report.
XOM's average geo contribution was substantially larger than all non-energy symbols.
No geo-conditioned forward outcomes were supplied.
proposals.risk: Over-aggressive clustering could merge distinct developments. The initial implementation should be observational and preserve the existing paper score.

proposals.title: Measure premarket bias, gaps, regime, and VIX against opening-window outcomes
proposals.current: Five premarket snapshots were all BULLISH with score 75 and small positive SPY/QQQ gaps. Social data were unavailable, XLF/FAS/FAZ gaps were missing, and later dashboard records showed zero premarket adjustment. No matched opening-window outcomes were provided.
proposals.proposed: For each scheduled premarket refresh, persist available gaps, missing-gap reasons, bias inputs, regime state, VIX level, geo score, social-source status, calculated adjustment, and actual application/expiry timestamps. Resolve SPY, QQQ, and trade-symbol returns at market open plus 5/15/30/60 minutes. Keep the current maximum adjustment, 60-minute active window, and 20-minute warmup unchanged until at least 12 resolved sessions or otherwise appropriate independent observations are available.
evidence: Premarket rows totaled only five and all had the same BULLISH classification.
SPY and QQQ gaps were +0.272% and +0.386%; financial ETF gaps were null.
Social source and status were UNAVAILABLE.
Regime observations were exclusively RISK_ON and VIX was 16.17, preventing separation of their effects without matched outcomes.
proposals.risk: Intraday observations from one session are correlated and must not be treated as independent daily samples. Instrumentation should distinguish sessions from refresh records.

proposals.title: Add ZPTA bar-freshness qualification and defer calibration
proposals.current: Each reported model/horizon cell has only 7 or 8 samples, no shadow trades closed, and the latest state was NO_NEW_BAR using yahoo_delayed data. Existing metrics do not state whether stale bars were included in evaluated predictions.
proposals.proposed: Record bar age, expected interval, provider latency, and freshness status for every ZPTA prediction. Mark stale or NO_NEW_BAR predictions as data-quality-ineligible for calibration while retaining them in an audit stream. Continue collecting fresh resolved predictions until each model/horizon under review has at least 12 eligible samples; leave the entry score of 68 and $150 shadow position limit unchanged.
evidence: Reported model sample sizes are below the minimum calibration target of 12.
Latest provider was yahoo_delayed and latest status was NO_NEW_BAR.
There were zero shadow trades and zero closed shadow trades, so no strategy-level P/L evidence exists.
proposals.risk: A strict freshness rule could reduce sample accumulation. It should therefore label and separate observations rather than stop the SHADOW collector.
